extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in international affairs
extracted.subtask_description: Newspaper/press reporting covering multiple international political and diplomatic developments (United Nations, European trade, Indonesian independence, etc.), summarizing events, agreements, and procedural conditions. Intended as multi-item international news coverage for a general readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sovereignty resolution ratification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The sovereignty resolution must be ratified by the Dutch and Indonesian Parliaments and by the representative bodies of the other fifteen constituent states of the republic of the U.S.I.; if one should refuse, these decisions would be invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ratification is expected; votes must occur within six weeks. Not later than December 30, the Queen is to proclaim the republic's sovereignty at a ceremony in her Amsterdam palace (contingent on ratification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dutch transfer of sovereignty timing and condition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Netherlands agreed 'unconditionally and irrevocably' to transfer complete sovereignty to the young republic not later than Dec. 30, provided the Dutch and Indonesian parliaments approve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfer is conditional on parliamentary approval; proclamation by the Queen scheduled if approvals occur. The agreement was framed to avoid failure of the round-table conference by compromising on contested items.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Guinea temporary status and dispute timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: New Guinea is to remain under Dutch control for another year pending further discussions, with the New Guinea question to be addressed and endeavored to be solved in 1950.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indonesians had wanted New Guinea included in the new United States of Indonesia but agreed to defer its status to preserve the broader agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of Dutch troops timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: The military agreement provides for withdrawal of all Dutch troops from Indonesia within the first six months of 1950 if shipping space permits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal is tied to logistical constraints (shipping space). The UN Conciliation Commission will cooperate in the withdrawal process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dutch naval withdrawal and base provisional status
rubrics_metrics.description: A one-year limit was set for withdrawal of the Dutch navy; the great naval base at Scerahaja (Java) will remain provisionally under the Dutch. When Indonesia emerges fully independent the base will have a Dutch commander responsible to the Indonesian government under the Indonesian flag.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naval withdrawal has a distinct timetable and transitional command arrangements for the major base; legal/administrative ties to the Dutch crown remain during the transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union cooperation scope between Netherlands and Indonesia
rubrics_metrics.description: The Netherlands–Indonesian union provides for limited Dutch and Indonesian co-operation in foreign relations, defense, economic and cultural matters and includes cooperation 'as far as necessary' in financial matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The union links the new state to the Dutch crown as an equal partner but creates tighter legal bonds than those holding together the British dominions; documents give all nations equal rights in Indonesia's economic activity and industrial development.

rubrics_metrics.name: UN Political Committee resolution on Greece (calls and instructions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A resolution (put up by Australia, China, Britain and the United States) calls on Bulgaria and Albania to cease immediately any further aid to the Greek guerrillas; calls for cessation of military operations in Greece; recommends a general amnesty; and instructs the special committee to continue its work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The resolution was turned down by Vishinsky in debate, but the resolution's substantive demands reflect the allied delegations' aims: stop external support for guerrillas, halt operations, and seek political reconciliation measures such as amnesty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Western European trade liberalization proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: France agreed to a British proposal freeing 50 per cent of Western European trade from import quotas, with member countries urging amendments to prevent the percentage from being applied automatically and to permit continued discrimination against some products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The council was reported to be moving toward approval; proposed safeguards (amendments) would limit automatic application and maintain quota protections on about 35% of trade with certain products where import quotas would otherwise be removed.
